linkedin.text:
Your assessor asks which AI agents you run, who owns each one, and who approved what they did. Where does the answer come from?

Control Tower v0.2.12 answers it from the gateway's own records. A new Compliance page (Enterprise) sets your coding assistants and agents against the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001. Each requirement is met, partly met, a gap, or the organisation's, computed from what Control Tower already sees: inventory, permissions, gates, approvals, logs, retention, the audit trail, single sign-on and alerts.

Concrete checks: every agent has an owner. Every active agent is limited to named models and tools. At least two people can approve, and nobody approves their own request. Calls are kept at least six months. The audit log's hash chain verifies.

The evidence pack is Markdown or JSON, and each download goes in the audit log with its SHA-256, so the assessor's copy can be checked.

Building in public: the day after release, an agent limited to no tools showed as wide open. An empty allow-list allows nothing; fixed on main.

Evidence for an assessment, not a certification or legal advice. The gateway underneath is open source and self-hosted: https://github.com/joshmaster2165/controltower

A ⭐ helps others find it.

#AIGovernance #AIAgents #OpenSource

posts:
Control Tower v0.2.12: a Compliance page that sets your AI agents and coding assistants against the EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF and ISO/IEC 42001.

Not a questionnaire. Each requirement's status is computed from what the gateway already records.

The checks are boring on purpose:

Every agent has an owner.
Every active agent is limited to named models and tools.
2+ approvers, nobody approves their own request.
Calls kept 6+ months.
The audit log's hash chain verifies.

The evidence pack is Markdown or JSON, and each download goes in the audit log with its SHA-256.

Found the day after release: an agent allowed no tools showed as wide open. An empty allow-list allows nothing. Fixed on main.

Compliance is in Enterprise; the gateway underneath is open source and self-hosted.

A star helps others find it ⭐ https://github.com/joshmaster2165/controltower

brief.notes: All claims from docs/changelog.md (0.2.12), docs/compliance.md and commit 50cedae. Compliance is Enterprise (ELv2) and the copy says so; the open-source gateway is what records the inventory, gates, approvals and hash-chained audit log it reads. The empty-allow-list fix (50cedae) is on main but not yet in a release, so the copy says 'fixed on main', not a version. 'Calls kept six months' = the Log retention check (CT_RETENTION_DAYS 183 or more, or 0). 'Not a certification or legal advice' is from the doc. Cards only: no recorder scene or still covers the Compliance page.
